surprises.head: Tampa Bay buried Minnesota in shots
surprises.body: Tampa Bay controls the shot count like almost no one else. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: Tampa Bay took 59 of the 83 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Tampa Bay would expect about 53%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

surprises.head: Minnesota couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Point reaches 700 points as the Lightning beat the Wild
paras: Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov scored just over two minutes apart early in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Marcus Foligno and Scott Sabourin squared off midway through the period. Jake Guentzel got the Lightning on the board on the power play late in the second. Shabanov scored his second of the night early in the third to make it 3-1 for the Wild. Guentzel struck again with a little over six minutes left to pull the Lightning within one, with Brayden Point picking up his 700th NHL point on the goal. With the goalie pulled and three and a half minutes left, Charle-Édouard D'Astous made it 3-3 on the power play. Nikita Kucherov won it on the power play in overtime. Two players had three-point nights: D'Astous with a goal and two assists, and Guentzel with two goals and an assist.
The Lightning carried the play, outshooting the Wild 34-22, but needed overtime to win it. Dennis Hildeby made 19 saves for the Bolts, and Calvin Pickard stopped 30 of 34 at the other end.
The Lightning went 3-for-6 on the power play. The Lightning moved to 11-3-2, third in the Atlantic, while the Wild dropped to 12-3-4, still first in the Central.
